objectives: Check out: Quiero dejar la habitación
Leave your suitcase at the hotel for the day
Ask reception to call a taxi
Say what you have to do: tengo que…

teach.es: Buenos días. Quiero dejar la habitación.
teach.en: Good morning. I'd like to check out.
teach.note: Literally 'I want to leave the room'. Check-out is usually at 12:00. Ask: ¿A qué hora tengo que dejar la habitación?

teach.es: Tengo que estar en el aeropuerto a las tres.
teach.en: I have to be at the airport at three.
teach.note: tengo que + verb = I have to… The same tener you know: tengo que pagar, tengo que ir.

teach.en: Can I leave my suitcase here?
teach.note: la maleta = suitcase. Almost every hotel will keep it after check-out, often free. Your Sunday flight to Marrakesh makes this useful.

teach.es: ¿Me pide un taxi para el aeropuerto?
teach.en: Could you call me a taxi to the airport?
teach.note: pide = you ask for, order (usted). Literally 'Will you ask for a taxi for me?'.

teach.md:
**Taxis in Madrid** are white with a red diagonal stripe. A green light on the roof means it's free.

Between the city centre (inside the M-30 ring road) and Barajas there's a **fixed fare**, whichever terminal. The price is shown inside the taxi. Apps like Uber and Cabify work too.

teach.es: ¿Me hace la factura a nombre de Smith?
teach.en: Can you make out the invoice to Smith?
teach.note: la factura = a full invoice with your name, for expenses. A simple receipt is el ticket or el recibo.

vocab.note: + verb: tengo que ir, tengo que pagar.

vocab.en: Can I leave my suitcase here?
Could you call me a taxi?
